sample_unit: interview participants (section leaders, researchers, department managers)

links.effect: Participants reported a lack of training; formal AI training is absent in Sweden and remains limited despite AI in workflows such as image reconstruction, protocol optimisation and patient positioning.
links.quote: Participants reported a lack of training and uncertainty about the future, as radiographers' roles are rarely considered in technology implementation.

links.outcome: Radiographer concerns about deskilling and loss of identity from AI
links.effect: Participants viewed AI as both a facilitator and a potential threat to core tasks, raising concerns about deskilling and loss of identity; maintaining competence was highlighted as critical.
links.quote: Participants viewed AI as both a facilitator of daily work and a potential threat to core tasks, raising concerns about deskilling and loss of identity.

unlisted_practices: Including radiographers in AI implementation planning and formalising AI education in undergraduate and postgraduate curricula

screen.reason: Qualitative multi-case interview study investigating radiographers' roles, experiences, and perceptions regarding real-world AI implementation across three university hospitals.
